newsitem.title: UK: New N.Ireland minister flies straight to Belfast.
newsitem.headline: New N.Ireland minister flies straight to Belfast.

text.p: Majorie Mowlam, Britain's new Northern Ireland secretary, on Saturday paid a flying visit to the capital of the troubled region just hours after being appointed by Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair.

Mowlam's main tasks are to revive the stalled Irish peace process and persuade the banned Irish Republican Army to declare a new ceasefire. She is the first woman to ever hold the post, one of trickiest jobs in British politics.
Mowlam was warmly greeted by well-wishers the second she stepped out of her official car in the centre of Belfast.

"It would be very naive to suggest that I can find solutions to problems very quickly but I think there is a sensitivity that needs to be shown and I will do my best to do that," she told a large crowd of reporters.
"I hope it is one of the advantages I might bring to the job," she added before setting off on a tour of the city centre, shaking hands with passers-by.

Her 10 predecessors all failed to bring lasting peace to the troubled province, where more than 3,000 people have died over the last 30 years in fighting between Protestants who want to stay part of Britain and Catholics who want the region to be united with Ireland.
